title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No substantive error. As written, the setup uses O_X where the relevant objects are local coordinates (étale maps), with A'(f,g) = dg/df valued in O_X^*. Grothendieck himself flags this in the margin and corrects it on the next page.

The surjectivity of d: O_X → ω_X depends on the analytic or C^∞ setting and on dim X = 1, as Grothendieck states. It fails Zariski-locally in the algebraic setting, and in characteristic p the kernel is O_X^p rather than the constants. This is relevant given that page 73 discusses characteristic p, but the page does not address it.

ideas.what: Differential invariants of subgroups of PGL_2 acting on the line (translations, homotheties/affine group, projective group), organized as group-invariant cocycles A(f,g) on pairs of local coordinates with axioms (cocycle, invariance, local rigidity, surjectivity).
ideas.modern_name: Hierarchy of (G,X)-structures on curves: translation structures (abelian differentials), affine structures (connections), projective structures (Schwarzian, torsor under quadratic differentials)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Poincaré); modern sheaf-theoretic treatment by Gunning (Lectures on Riemann Surfaces, 1966; 'Special coordinate coverings', 1967) and Deligne (Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers, 1970)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; this cote 93 material is unpublished notes

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism O_X/C ≅ ω_X via d, for X smooth of dimension 1 in analytic or C^∞ settings, i.e. the torsor attached to the translation group is trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Holomorphic Poincaré lemma / exactness of 0 → C → O_X → Ω^1_X → 0 on curves
ideas.where_published: Standard (de Rham comparison in Grothendieck 1966 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties')

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a routine first step of a survey: the translation-group analogue of the Schwarzian/projective-structure discussion, which is classical (Gunning, Deligne). The axiomatic 'invariant cocycle' framing is a nice pedagogical unification, but it contains no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: Heading line 'a) Groupe des translations. Cas virtuel[?] sur E^1[?]' more plausibly reads 'a) Groupe des translations, G_a opérant sur E^1'. This parallels the next page's 'b) Groupe opérant sur E^1 ou E^{1*} ≃ G_m par homothéties'.
'(ab marchant[?] vrai aussi dans l'analytique réel...' likely reads '(cela marchant aussi dans l'analytique réel ou le C^∞, ou C^3)'.

Line after d: O_X → ω_X: the crossed-out 'tuée exactement' is replaced by the insertion 'épi (X lisse de dim 1) et'. The sentence reads 'épi (X lisse de dim 1) et qui est tuée exactement sur les fonctions loc. constantes'.
Marginal note likely reads: 'Ici O_X mauvais choix, E_X plutôt!' (E_X = sheaf of local coordinates/étale maps). The next page confirms this with 'Si on s'intéresse à E_X au lieu de O_X'.
The final lines are partly illegible. Plausibly: 'Il est pas la peine d'introduire de torseur, ω = A(f,g), on l'exprimera de façon ... dans les cas qui nous occupent' (uncertain).
